questions.statement: Which of the following is an uncountable noun?

options.feedback: Incorrect. You can count carrots.
Correct! Sugar is a substance and is uncountable.
Incorrect. You can count bananas.
Incorrect. You can count eggs.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies basic noun countability categories.

questions.statement: What is the superlative form of the adjective "cheap"?

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is the comparative.
Correct! Short adjectives add -est and use "the".
Incorrect. "Cheap" is a short adjective.
Incorrect form.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the correct superlative form for a short adjective.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "I have ________ books in my bag, so it is not very heavy."
questions.context: Using quantifiers for a small number.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Books are countable.
Correct! "A few" is for a small number of countable items.
Incorrect. Used for uncountable.
Incorrect. "Many" would make the bag heavy.

questions.explanation:
The student understands the correct quantifier based on countability and contextual logic.

questions.statement: "We ________ have a picnic if the weather is good next Sunday."

options.feedback: Incorrect. Missing "to".
Correct! Future plan/intention.
Incorrect. "We" requires "are".
Incorrect. Missing the verb "to be".

questions.explanation:
The student understands the structural requirements for the "going to" future.

questions.statement: "This new phone is ________ than my old one." (Adjective: expensive)

options.feedback: Incorrect. Long adjectives don't take -er.
Correct! Comparative form for a long adjective.
Incorrect. Use comparative for two things.
Incorrect. Missing the second "as".

questions.explanation:
The student applies comparative rules for long adjectives.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which item did they buy the most of?
questions.context:
A description of a family's grocery shopping.
"We bought many oranges and a few pineapples. We also bought some rice and a bottle of oil. We didn't buy any meat because we already had some at home."

options.feedback: Correct! They bought "many" oranges vs "a few" pineapples.
Incorrect. They only bought "a few".
Incorrect. They didn't buy "any".
Incorrect. "Some" is general, but "many" for oranges suggests a larger count.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to compare quantities expressed with different quantifiers.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "I ________ forget to bring your book tomorrow, I promise!"

options.feedback: Incorrect. You wouldn't promise to forget.
Correct! "Won't" is the negative future used for a promise not to do something.
Incorrect. Missing "going to".
Incorrect. Not the standard tense for a specific future promise.

questions.explanation:
The student applies the future auxiliary "will" (negative form) to express a promise.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is LOGICALLY and GRAMMATICALLY correct?
questions.context: Analyzing comparative and superlative forms of irregular adjectives.

options.text: Pizza is the better food in the world.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Needs the superlative "best".

options.text: Fruits are more good for your health than candy.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Comparative of "good" is "better".

options.text: Vegetables are better for your health than candy.
options.feedback: Correct! "Better" is the correct comparative of "good".

options.text: Candy is the bestest food for your teeth.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Bestest" is not a word; "best" is already superlative.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the correct use of irregular comparative and superlative forms.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Whose plan is the most certain and pre-arranged?
questions.context:
Comparing three plans based on certainty.
"Mateo: I think I'll go to the park. / Ana: I am going to the park at 4 PM. / Luis: I might go to the park later."

options.feedback: Incorrect. "I think I'll" is a spontaneous/uncertain future.
Correct! "I am going" (present continuous for future) or "I am going to go" shows a firm plan with a specific time.
Incorrect. "Might" shows low certainty.
Incorrect. The different structures show different levels of commitment.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the nuances of future structures to determine the level of certainty or arrangement.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which evaluation best captures the essence of the text?
questions.context:
Evaluating an argument about healthy living.
"Living a healthy life is easier than most people think. It's not about being the best athlete, but about being better than you were yesterday. Small steps, like eating more fruit, are better than no steps at all."

options.text: Only the best athletes can be healthy.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says it's NOT about that.

options.text: Improvement and consistency are more important than perfection in healthy living.
options.feedback: Correct! "Better than you were yesterday" and "small steps" emphasize progress over perfection.

options.text: Eating fruit is the only way to be healthy.
options.feedback: Incorrect. It is mentioned as a "small step" example.

options.text: Healthy living is the most difficult task for humans.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says it is "easier than most people think".

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the central message and tone of a short motivational text about health.
